study_type_evidence.quote: The PK properties of 6 were measured in both mice and rats and compared with liraglutide.

in_vivo_species.quote: Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats (male, 200-250 g) and Kunming mice (male, 25-30 g) were purchased from Qinglongshan Animal Breeding Farm

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: male Kunming, 25-30 g; db/db C57BL/6 for efficacy

agents.name: Liraglutide
agents.sequence_source: Not printed in the body; sequence is PEPlife2's and is the native GLP-1(7-37) backbone of liraglutide. The palmitoyl-Glu protractor is not encoded.
agents.dose_route_quote: liraglutide (s.c.) was quickly removed from the circulation of Kunming mice and SD rats
agents.tmax: ~2.0 h in rats; ~1.8 h in mice
agents.pk_quote: liraglutide (s.c.) was quickly removed from the circulation of Kunming mice and SD rats with a half-life (t1/2) of 3.6 ± 0.2 h and 4.2 ± 0.3 h, respectively

agents.name: Analogue 6
agents.sequence_source: Not printed in the body; PEPlife2's string is a head-to-tail DIMER of a 40-residue exendin-4-like analogue, consistent with the paper's discussion of dimerization.
agents.dose_route_quote: The PK properties of 6 were measured in both mice and rats and compared with liraglutide.
agents.tmax: ~6.0 h in rats; ~4.7 h in mice
agents.auc: 7244.0 ± 928.8 in rats; 13715.2 ± 792.0 in mice (AUCinf, units not recoverable from the PDF text)
agents.pk_quote: the t1/2 of 6 was 10.8 ± 0.8 h in mice and 12.9 ± 3.6 h in rats, representing a ~ 2-fold increase than that of liraglutide

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: As shown in Figures 4A and B, liraglutide (s.c.) was quickly removed from the circulation of Kunming mice and SD rats
concentration_time_figure.note: Panel A is mouse and panel B is rat; both after subcutaneous dosing.

bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS, per PEPlife2's Assay field; the accepted-manuscript PDF text does not describe the bioanalysis in a recoverable form
notes: Read from the publisher PDF (an accepted manuscript, so the text carries interleaved 'ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT' watermark lines). Both PEPlife2 values verified exactly against the Results text: liraglutide 4.2 ± 0.3 h and analogue 6 12.9 ± 3.6 h in SD rats, both at 50 nmol/kg s.c. Two notes for downstream use. (1) Tmax is 2.0 h for liraglutide and 6.0 h for analogue 6, and both are subcutaneous, so part of the 3-fold half-life difference is slower absorption rather than slower clearance - the paper says so directly ('a slower absorption pattern of 6'). No intravenous arm is reported, so absorption and elimination cannot be separated. (2) PEPlife2's sequence for analogue 6 is a head-to-tail dimer of a 40-residue exendin-4-like sequence, consistent with the paper's dimerization strategy; liraglutide's string is the bare GLP-1 backbone with no palmitoyl protractor, so the lipidation that drives liraglutide's own half-life is absent from its representation.
